back: Shelling, sorting, roasting, removing skins, grinding, packaging.
Processing a raw product (groundnuts) into a product of higher value (peanut butter, oil).
To develop flavour and colour, drive off moisture, loosen the skins and kill microorganisms.
They may contain aflatoxins (liver poisons), which roasting does not destroy completely.
Sheller, winnowing basket, roaster, peanut butter making machine, grinding stone (guyo/imbokodo), mortar and pestle.
To keep out oxygen (rancid oil), moisture (moulds), dust and insects.

front: How is oil obtained from peanut butter?
back: Warm it, press it in a cloth bag; oil runs through the cloth; let it settle and decant or filter it.
Cooking and frying, margarine, soap, skin creams and hair oils, lamp fuel.

front: Physical and chemical changes in peanut processing
back: Shelling, grinding and pressing are physical changes; roasting and oil going rancid are chemical changes.
